about: The security class (controller ruling 2026-11-01, F7 (a)): a lane whose tree differs from develop's at a path matching a glob in `paths`, or at a path holding a `tokens` word anywhere (case-folded), takes a cold Opus read before the familiar's --no-ff merge lands. The familiar asks from the landing bench, whose tree stands at develop: `node tools/cold-read-owed.mjs <lane-ref>` pins the bench's HEAD and the lane head once, compares the two trees (`git diff-tree -r --no-renames --ignore-submodules=none --raw -z <base> <lane>`), and matches with this file and the matcher (packages/lararium-tw5/src/filters/security-class.ts) as develop's git objects hold them, never the lane's and never a daemon's. It prints `COLD READ OWED: <paths>` or `cold read: none owed`, then a record hash over the head, the base, this file's sha256 and the owed paths; a judge that cannot read answers `COLD READ OWED: (unread: <why>)`, never clean. The familiar records the read under that hash and quotes it in the merge message (`Cold-Read: <hash>`). This file sits in its own list, and the judge reads unread wherever the list stops owing its own path. The code that decides CI's verdict (cells, shards, witnesses, the build stamp, every manifest and test config) sits in the class too. Prune from evidence; never widen a hole.
